# Native Qwen client evidence

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The ignored collector compares all nine imported source/resource files against that commit before calling the unchanged public `QwenSpeechClient`. Maintained production code and checks use Rust without an interpreter or reference client.

`released-qwen.json` contains 178 independent sessions, including 119 observed transcription requests, 163 runtime starts and eleven device probes. SHA-256: `af43e7d1c1dd9080e30b9bce6da6177e4ae75b6bca506587a8f36868c4bd1781`. Both implementations start actual isolated child processes and use genuine loopback HTTP. The child is a synthetic native runtime serving controlled responses; sparse files satisfy the released model-readiness checks. This fixture does not run model inference.

The comparison records process arguments, inherited environment, null standard streams, private key/directory modes, bearer authentication, health retry, exact request-body hashes and decoded audio-block hashes/headers. Normalization removes only random port, owned root/temp paths and process IDs. No key value enters the fixture. The native client preserves the pinned Qwen 1.7B paths, offline/cache settings, four-thread CPU arguments, forced-language assistant prefix, automatic language mode, 25-second PCM16 blocks and memory-only WAV encoding. All thirty supported language names and ISO-639-1/3 mappings are exercised; result metadata preserves the requested language code.

Fragmented streams cover prefix hiding, previous-block provisional text, Unicode character limits, line bounds, nullable/malformed events, empty choices, length finishes, required completion markers, early EOF, HTTP failures and redirect refusal. Forty-six WAV-reader cases compare malformed/truncated/extensible inputs with and without runtime retention. Distinct format/EOF failures retain the released diagnostics and keep-alive behavior; ordinary input/runtime failures close the process. A shared native WAV-reader repair preserves that distinction without staging Incognito audio on disk.

Keep-alive reuse, close/restart, cancellation before readiness and after a callback, process exit, and forced termination observe real process disappearance and key removal. Closing during startup must return promptly instead of waiting for health readiness. Two concurrent cancel calls each observe the already reaped process and deleted key when returning. The startup regression demonstrably failed with the lifecycle lock held across health checks, exceeding the bounded twenty-second harness; releasing the lock after registering the actor passes the unchanged source observation. Earlier malformed-WAV and invalid GPU-stderr controls also failed before their owning repairs.

Device observations preserve the existing `cuda` setting name and Vulkan/NVIDIA selection, including Unicode decimal suffixes, CR/LF normalization, rejection of other vendors/backend names, invalid stdout/stderr and probe failure. The actual fifteen-second probe deadline is exercised. Probe timeout/cancellation drains or kills and reaps its owned child before reporting failure. This is simulated device discovery, not evidence of a physical GPU route.

The full workspace passes 104 ordinary native tests after the three-model scope change. The Qwen table is one integration test; the additional settings test exercises persisted retirement and saving. Formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Three isolated GTK tests, the installed-Codex comparison and the real pinned-runtime download test retain their previously executed separate evidence. A sixth ignored test now has separate [actual CPU/NVIDIA inference evidence](qwen-inference-evidence.md). `qwen-fixture-peer` is a development binary and must never ship. Its parent-death signal protects only fixture processes and does not establish production crash cleanup.

The ninety-second startup and full 180-second streaming deadlines, actual 5 GB RSS overflow, arbitrary malformed/nonstandard input, abrupt application crash, broader recognition-quality coverage, controller/session integration and complete app workflows remain required acceptance work. Physical CPU/GPU acceptance is now demonstrated on the public English/Chinese clips described in the separate evidence, not established by this synthetic table. No microphone, host model store, credentials, user content or visible desktop was used by these synthetic checks. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0; these checks establish client/process contracts, not full parity or a performance improvement.
